title: What Teen Parenting Is and Why It Matters
summary: The foundations of teen parenting: what it is and why getting it right pays off.
body:
Teens (13-19) need: autonomy with guardrails, sleep (8-10 hrs), and a parent who listens more than lectures. The goal is a launched adult, not a controlled child.

Why it matters: Teens need 8-10 hours of sleep (biology, not laziness) The prefrontal cortex develops until ~25

title: Getting Started: Your First Five Moves in Teen Parenting
summary: Start teen parenting this week with five concrete moves.
body:
Don't try to do everything. Do these five, in order:

1. Shift from control to influence
2. Set 3-5 non-negotiable rules
3. Negotiate the rest together
4. Keep communication lines open (car rides work)
5. Monitor without spying (know friends, plans)

Five moves, one week. Momentum beats perfection — the rest of this guide builds on exactly this start.
facts: Keep communication lines open (car rides work)

title: Teen Parenting Beginner FAQ
summary: Straight answers to the most common teen parenting questions.
body:
Q: How strict?
A: Few firm rules (safety, respect), flexibility elsewhere.

Q: Phone rules?
A: No phones at meals/bedtime; know the passcode for safety.

Q: When to worry?
A: Withdrawal, grade cliffs, friend changes - ask, don't accuse.

title: Teen Parenting: Safety, Legal, and Fine Print

body:
Read before you act: Lecturing instead of listening And: No sleep boundaries

General rules: get agreements in writing, understand what you're signing, keep records of money in and out, and know when a professional (lawyer, accountant, vet, doctor — depending on the domain) is worth the fee. An hour of professional advice beats a month of fixing.
